review_reference: Owner decisions of 18 Nov 2026 on hid-system#258 (Akos EHR plan, Release A, lane D): ORD-2 'activated prescriptions go automatically to the hospital's own pharmacy: YES' and 'pharmacy and lab staff get their own facility's work items only, never the chart'; Q102 'a fictional QA pharmacist and lab worker at QA Hospital, sealed QA only' (QA-1). Contract: docs/INTERFACE_CONTRACT.md, the 0133 and 0134 sections. This branch's own declaration, for its own checks: it names exactly 0133, 0134 and runtime-grants.sql. The hand-over on #258 (Rahman integrates 0128-0137) replaces it with one combined declaration for that release. To be signed by the owner.
evidence: DRAFT, not signed: the owner's review and signature are still to come, and the release integrator (#258) replaces this branch's declaration with one combined declaration for 0128-0137 (exactly those files plus the merged runtime-grants.sql, with its new sha256). Migrations 0133_own_facility_pharmacy_and_lab_work.sql (sha256 658cd4c77dfdc0fa25d55bfd40eea4f94a7eda8c3cb39c1e6d6baee80b6502f3) and 0134_sealed_qa_hospital_pharmacy_lab_staff.sql (sha256 13a58405e179befac7eb3e1854862b33787e040177a48fa98f55557b2cedb5b7) and their runtime-grants.sql block (file sha256 5a317cafa40bf8e94c032398af4bd01405b6468089b2cb7d4cd36c3b391ba3e3; it grants the two halves of the own-work member test to the Lab and Pharmacy runtimes, ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed to the EHR runtime, and revokes the withdrawal trigger function from PUBLIC). WHAT 0133 DOES: the own-work member test, in two halves: identity.facility_work_session_membership (a staff session that set app.own_facility_work to '0133', which only the new lab-api, pharmacy-api and ehr-api images do, in every staff transaction (the owner's Q120 B; in ehr-api it only switches the order-route send and its resend flag to D14's rule); direct care, the session's facility, <kind>.work-item.read and <kind>.order-route.receive held there through an active membership, which today only the pharmacist and lab roles hold; it answers that membership, or null) and the row's half, one per kind (identity.pharmacy_work_patient_allows for the Pharmacy runtime only, identity.lab_work_patient_allows for the Lab runtime only; STRICT, given that membership: still the session's, at the row's facility, active and not on hold, of an active account whose subject is the session's actor; the patient on D15's list of patients with own work of that kind at that facility; the patient active; no deny directive covering that member), and whole as identity.facility_work_member_allows; called on its own by its runtime, the row's half answers only for a patient on its own kind's list at that facility (the owner's Q122 A closes #280's Q4: before, it answered for any patient id the caller held, and one shared row's half let each runtime ask about the other kind); the work items gain a read policy for own items (no order route), and the work chain 42 policies decided item by item, the path to the own work item read in the policy itself by the querying role: 44 permissive policies named staff_own_work_*, which sort after every lab_* and pharmacy_* policy, so PostgreSQL (which joins permissive policies with OR in reverse name order) asks them first; each asks the session's half once per statement (one InitPlan) and, for every other session, never calls the row's half or reads the path; 0124's patient cards gain the test; 0086's context_allows and work_item_allows are unchanged, so the imported evidence, the Lab outbox and the route reports gain nothing and a route-backed item's rows never pass; pharmacy.own_prescription_sends (row-level security on, no policy, no grant); ehr.send_prescription_to_own_pharmacy for the EHR runtime (pharmacy-api's own PharmacyWorkItemCreated payload; after a dispensing it answers that the pharmacy already has the prescription) and ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed (its no_pharmacy test alone, read only, for the prescription list and page; it asks the full permission check of pharmacy staff only); the withdrawal: a trigger on ehr.prescriptions (prescriptions_own_pharmacy_send_withdrawn, its SECURITY DEFINER function the owner's alone) records a sent prescription held, cancelled, entered in error, edited or resumed whichever ehr-api image changes it, and ehr.withdraw_own_pharmacy_send and the pharmacy list's states report it only while the item is not dispensed; the own-work access check answers the audit basis (consent for a member holding its own grant for the action, else own-work, as the list's reader does); two ehr.prescriptions policies for the dispensing validator's owner only; D14 (the owner's Q121 A): until the hospital's own pharmacy has dispensed it, the prescriber may send the prescription to an outside pharmacy, and the own item is withdrawn as sent elsewhere (it leaves the hospital pharmacy's list and cannot be dispensed there); after an own dispensing the send still answers ORDER_ROUTE_ORDER_IN_WORK; pharmacy.work_items' unique(source_ehr_prescription_id) and unique(source_ehr_prescription_id, source_ehr_prescription_version) become one unique index on (source_ehr_prescription_id, order_route_id is not null), one own item and one route-backed item per prescription; pharmacy.prescription_item_claims (owner-only: row-level security on, no policy, no grant) records each item's claim on its prescription, at most one live, kept by two ENABLE ALWAYS triggers on pharmacy.work_items and pharmacy.dispensings (and two more that refuse, in every session, a change of an item's prescription, route, facility or id or of a dispensing's item), so that for every image a released (sent-elsewhere) own item can never be dispensed (23514 PRESCRIPTION_SOURCE_NOT_DISPENSABLE, DETAIL sent_elsewhere) and no prescription is dispensed twice; ehr.send_order_route and ehr.order_route_resend_allowed are replaced with 0123's and 0086's text plus hunks marked 0133 D14 that release the undispensed own claim (one of them edits a 0123 condition in place), reached only by a session that set the switch (the new ehr-api sets it in staff transactions), so without it both answer as 0123 and 0086 do; pharmacy.own_withdrawn_work_items() lists the facility's withdrawn own item ids and reasons for the new pharmacy-api's list; D15 (the owner's Q122 A): identity.own_work_patients (owner-only) lists the patients with own work per kind and facility, kept by two ENABLE ALWAYS triggers (one on each work item table, one shared function) and filled once by 0133's backfill. UNDO (by hand only, in one transaction): restore 0123's ehr.send_order_route and 0086's ehr.order_route_resend_allowed first, so nothing more is sent elsewhere; then drop the withdrawal trigger, its function and the other readers of the sends table before the table, or every later prescription status or version change fails (42P01); D14's claims table, its four triggers and the key change are never dropped (without them a sent-elsewhere own item could be dispensed next to the outside one); D15 and D1's halves go last; 0133's header gives the order. WHAT 0134 DOES: where 0123 installed the sealed QA tenant (Amazon RDS: production and staging) the QA Pharmacist and QA Lab Scientist logins gain a pharmacist and a lab membership at QA Hospital; a login that is not 0123's now, or one the QA Facility Admin already gave that role at QA Hospital (active or not), is left alone with a notice instead of stopping the release; elsewhere nothing. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's images call none of the new functions and never set app.own_facility_work, so the session's half answers them null and through the changed policies, D2 and 0124's cards they list, read, write and record exactly what they do on 0001-0127 (their pharmacy and lab staff still need a consent grant; the cards and audit rows stay as 0124 gives them); either image can therefore be deployed, or rolled back alone, after 0133 (the owner's Q120 B), and while today's pharmacy-api serves (a rollback of it alone, or a rollout in which the new ehr-api serves first), a prescription the new ehr-api sends to the hospital's own pharmacy is answered as sent, reaches its pharmacists only through a consent grant and the new ehr-api can still send it to an outside pharmacy before it is dispensed (D14), but today's pharmacy-api then keeps the sent-elsewhere item on its list as open work, refuses its dispensing (409) and answers its progress as received, so pharmacy-api goes out with or before ehr-api; today's ehr-api never sets the switch, so its send keeps 0123's rule (ORDER_ROUTE_ORDER_IN_WORK once the hospital pharmacy has the prescription) and, after a rollback of ehr-api alone, also for a prescription already sent elsewhere whose route was then declined, until the new ehr-api is back; D14's claim triggers and D15's list trigger run for every image (D15 keys its list by work item, so today's images' concurrent acceptances never meet on it); today's images pay COST's planning cost too (the planner cannot know the switch); the withdrawal is the database's, so today's ehr-api images mark it too; ehr-api answers ownPharmacyStaffed and pharmacyHandoff only where 0133 is applied. LOCKS: 0133 takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.prescriptions, lab.work_items, pharmacy.work_items and the 20 chain tables that gain a policy (and ACCESS SHARE on the four identity tables and auth.accounts, which its SQL functions and its post-check of the send read, 28 tables, plus the three tables it creates, and auth.accounts' indexes, by planning a query on it under a 10 ms lock_timeout) NOWAIT; first in its transaction (the runner applies each file in its own) it retries every 100 ms for at most 5 s, else 55P03 with nothing of 0133 applied; when its transaction already holds another migration's table locks (the runner's dry run of 0128-0137 in one transaction) it makes one attempt and no sleep; in that dry run the locks of every file last until it ends, so every Lab and Pharmacy work list and chain read waits meanwhile, and a later file that waited for its own locks (up to the runner's 5 s lock_timeout) would keep them held (0136 takes its locks NOWAIT with one attempt inside a dry run since 2940d1a0, as 0133 does, so it does not wait that way), which the combined declaration must state for any file that does (the dry run belongs in a quiet window). 0134 writes at most two rows in each of two tables, only where the QA tenant is installed. COST: lab-api's work list for a busy laboratory (1,050 work items, the database-migration job's runtime check, which runs with a superuser owner), in two runs at ef45a60a: 7.6-8.1 s for the consent-backed clinician (8.4-8.5 s in two earlier runs on 0133 a41f5796, whose function bodies are the same; earlier builds of 0133 in this branch 7.7-8.7 s; 0001-0127 about 7.2 s, in one earlier run whose log was not kept; the same 5,631 consent checks) and 1.5-1.6 s for the lab scientist without a grant (1.7 s in those runs; 1.3-1.5 s in runs of builds before D15), the same 200 rows, under lab-api's 15 s limit; auth.membership_has_permission 16 and 74 times per statement. With every table owned by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, as in production, on one throwaway cluster, interleaved with 0133 at 8f42aba4 (before D14 and D15), 24 runs each, at ef45a60a: the lab scientist's list at the laboratory's 4,010 lab work items 3.9 s median (3.1-4.4 s; at 8f42aba4 3.6 s, 3.0-3.9 s), 93,314 row's-half calls per statement either way; the pharmacist's list at the pharmacy's 3,001 items 0.42-0.56 s with today's query and with the new pharmacy-api's 0133 query alike (at 8f42aba4 0.43-0.53 s). Measured on an earlier build of this branch (round g, before the switch, D14, D15 and the per-kind halves) and not repeated: the lab scientist 2.1-2.3 s at 2,000 lab items; the consent-backed clinician 13.2-14.4 s at 2,000 (0001-0127 on the same kit 12.4-14.0 s; JIT now compiles it, about 0.6 s; 0086's consent test on every row of the laboratory's history reaches the limit at about 2,200 items whatever 0133 does); the list reads the laboratory's whole history, and from about 5,000 items PostgreSQL's JIT adds about 3.4 s, because the own-work policies raise the list's estimated cost about 40 times; by extrapolation from runs at 4,000 to 8,000 items, about 15,000 items would reach the limit with jit on (PostgreSQL's default) and about 19,000 with jit off, not measured at those sizes; a lab result's verification insert 0.16 s. The owner's Q123 A makes the lists read open work plus the last 90 days, after Release A. The first form of the own-work policies (a chain function asking the whole test on every row, d724af0c) failed the job at lab-api's 15 s limit (57014; without the limit it took about 22 s and 19 s, in a run whose log was not kept). no row without it; the clinician 7.6-8.1 s). Mutations: each of 21 mutations of D14, D15, the per-kind halves, D10's reader and the grants makes the own-facility suite fail (run on a database whose function bodies match 21b1eed0's pins; the database files have changed since only in 0133's header comments). Independent adversarial review after each round (nine so far; the ninth, before publishing, checked every claim of this declaration, #280's description and its #258 post against the logs and the code, and found the header's wrong isolation level for pharmacy-api's dispensing, its stale note on 0136, cost figures not labelled with their build and the runtime verifiers' teardown race, all fixed; the eighth reviewed Q121 A's and Q122 A's build with five lenses (the dispensing invariant, today's images, privacy, the services, tests and docs) after the seventh attacked their design: the row's half split per kind, the claim keys immutable even in replica mode, D15 keyed per own item, and SERIALIZABLE on the own send reverted because 0117's allergy check would then miss an allergy recorded after the transaction's first statement; the sixth of the switch: every own-work path goes through the session's half, which suite case 7h shows for today's image unset and empty, another value, PH and LS without it and PG with grants the same either way, and each of its probes fails with the switch removed); the three before it of the session-once policies: a statement that changes its session settings partway reads nothing more, on the Lab and Pharmacy work items and a chain table of each (suite case 7g, each probe failing on an unbound row's half whatever the statistics, shown on the row's half before its split per kind), only the session's own member of the facility's pharmacy or lab staff reads own work through the policies, the row's half asks on each row only what a statement can change, and the Pharmacy policies are asked first (case 7g compares the consent checks; section 8 holds the name order). TO COMPLETE: the owner's review and signature (reviewed_by); the owner's answers on #280's open question (whether a change after a dispensing should reach the pharmacy); after Release A, as the owner decided: several outside pharmacies sharing one prescription's quantity (Q119, its own project) and work lists of open work plus the last 90 days (Q123 A, lab-api and pharmacy-api, no migration); the coordinator's answers recorded: OWN_WORK_PATIENT_CARD_ENABLED is off in production (so the new images read no cards there), a NOTICE is enough for an existing QA Hospital membership, and the per-file apply is acceptable if today's images are checked between files in the integration rehearsal; and the combined declaration above, whose integrator re-checks that 0128-0132 neither replace work_item_allows nor lock the two work item tables. COLLATION: 0133's post-checks compare its sends table's constraint and index lists and the own-work policies' names in a fixed order (COLLATE "C"), so they hold whatever the database's default collation is; proved at ef45a60a by the job's runtime check, which applies 0001-0134 with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds (as the database-migration image test does) on a cluster whose default collation is ICU en-US (the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image uses libc en_US.utf8; both order text by language rules, unlike C), where every post-check passes, and by all 102 database suites (17 + 85) on a superuser build applied by the runner on such a cluster.
